name: Develop
description:
Multi-agent development pipeline: Planner dispatches Dev + Tests in parallel, Docs writes it up, QA merges and opens a draft pull/merge request.

Gated on the "conduit-dev" label — Analyze applies it to auto-chain an opened issue into a draft PR; re-apply it to re-run.

On completion QA swaps the label to "conduit-review" to hand off to Review. Projects users who prefer drag-to-column can swap the trigger to status=Dev; GitLab boards are label-native out of the box.

workflows.name: Develop
workflows.description: Polling on label=conduit-dev. Planner reads the ticket and dispatches scoped work to Dev and Tests (parallel branched worktrees). Docs runs once both finish so it documents what was actually shipped. QA consumes the merged workspace, opens a draft pull/merge request, and swaps the issue label conduit-dev → conduit-review.

nodes.name: Planner
nodes.instructionsAppend: Convention for this workflow: Dev owns production code only, Tests owns test files only. (Docs and QA run after the parallel group and are not part of your dispatch.) If this issue already has a linked draft pull/merge request carrying a "changes requested" review (a loop-back from Review), read that PR's latest review feedback first via the connected MCP server and scope Dev's and Tests' work to addressing it.

nodes.name: Dev
nodes.instructionsAppend: Sibling agent Tests runs in parallel — do not touch test files. Docs runs after you finish — do not touch user-facing documentation. Focus only on production code.

nodes.name: Docs
nodes.instructionsAppend: Your workspace already contains the merged output of Dev and Tests. Document only what was actually implemented — read the diff and `.conduit/` summaries from upstream agents before writing.

nodes.name: QA
nodes.instructionsAppend: On a loop-back from Review, reuse the existing draft pull/merge request for this branch/issue if one already exists — only open a new PR when none does. After opening or reusing the PR, apply the "conduit-review" label to it in prose via the connected MCP server (you just created or found it, so no lookup beyond the trigger is needed). The final writeback step applies "conduit-review" to the linked issue and removes the consumed "conduit-dev"; do not change the issue's status.
